title: COORDINATED ENTRY RESEARCH ANALYST
desc: The Human Resources Administration (HRA) is dedicated to fighting poverty and income inequality by providing New Yorkers in need with essential benefits such as Food Assistance and Emergency Rental Assistance. As the largest local social services agency in the country, HRA helps more than three million New Yorkers annually through the administration of more than 15 major public assistance programs. Housing Services Administration is a division of New York City’s Department of Social Services that oversees housing stability and rehousing efforts. HSA administers rental assistance, housing supply, and placement programs to help individuals and families exit shelter, prevent homelessness, and secure safe, affordable housing across the city. The Office of Supportive Housing and Specialized Services helps formerly homeless clients succeed in the community by providing access to permanent housing with support services. Supportive Housing and Specialized Services works closely with other divisions of DSS/HRA/DHS and with other governmental and non-governmental providers to create new programs and to integrate and refine existing services so that clients experiencing homelessness and those at risk can move into safe, affordable housing that best supports their stability and integration in the community. Program areas under Supportive Housing & Specialized Services purview include the Coordinated Entry Unit which oversees the Coordinated Assessment and Placement System (CAPS). CAPS serves as NYC’s Coordinated Entry system per the HUD mandate to ensure that localities use a coordinated system to assure systematic and timely referral and placement of homeless and at-risk clients into the most appropriate permanent housing programs. CAPS includes assessment services for individuals/families potentially eligible for supportive housing or rental assistance programs; an application system to determine supportive housing eligibility; a rapid-rehousing request, referral and enrollment module; an electronic referral component; and a vacancy control system to verify and monitor placements. The Office of Supportive Housing and Specialized Services is recruiting for one (1) City Research Scientist II to function as a Research Analyst who will support the Director of Coordinated Entry and the Senior Research Analyst by providing research and evaluation to inform the development and implementation of the CAPS Coordinated Entry system and who will: - Perform evaluation and research using descriptive, process and outcomes data from CAPS to identify operational efficiencies, assess model fidelity, and inform the development of operational performance measures; this includes extracting CAPS information by writing non-automated SQL and SPSS code and reviewing, quantifying, and analyzing data using various research methodologies. - Support DSS/HRA supportive housing policy directives and respond to data and analytic requests from leadership and external stakeholders by: designing, executing and analyzing analyses of CAPS data; developing non-automated ad hoc SQL code for extraction and analysis of complex data sets; designing, preparing and presenting data visualizations; and disseminating research findings beyond the unit through writing memos and reports including Local Law submissions and creating and delivering presentations. - Monitor administrative CAPS data for survey, application, determination, rapid-rehousing, and vacancy control modules; make and record observations, including developing new recording systems; design and prepare visualizations and communicate findings to internal and external stakeholders. - Prepare responses to legal and media requests, including creating non-automated SQL code to extract and analyze CAPS data. - Support Federal reporting to HUD; validate, troubleshoot, and upload file sets extracted from CAPS into NYC's HMIS data warehouse; collaborate with the Office of Business Strategies and Solutions to refine file generation logic as needed. - Conduct data sharing in support of intra- and interagency research and evaluation efforts. - Perform literature and data reviews to evaluate the validity and reliability of prior studies and reports to be used in formulating research questions and future report methodologies. - Perform other related duties as directed. Hours/Schedule: Monday-Friday 9am-5pm CITY RESEARCH SCIENTIST - 21744 1. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey's brand team has built a creative agent that makes on-brand work on request: ads, social posts, decks, product films, and tailored demo videos for prospects. It reads our brand guidelines and design system live, works in the same tools our designers use, and hands back files a designer can open and keep editing.

We're hiring a senior engineer to own it. You'll spend most of your time building the agent and some of it making real work with it, because shipping with it is the fastest way to find what's broken. You'll report to our Creative Director and work closely with the designers, marketers, and sales teams who use the agent every day.

By the end of your first year, account executives and marketers make the work they need, on brand, without waiting on a designer.

 - Own the creative agent end to end: its skills, templates, tool connections, and the quality of what it makes

 - Turn how our designers work into reusable recipes, so a request for an ad or a demo video comes back as work a Creative Director would approve

 - Build and run the media pipelines behind our films and ads, including rendering, video and audio processing, voiceover, music, and generated imagery

 - Write evals that catch off-brand copy, layout, and numbers before anyone sees them

 - Make the agent dependable for people who aren't designers, with clear questions when something is missing and recovery when a tool fails

 - Ship creative work with the agent every week, and feed what you learn back into it

 - Decide with the Creative Director what to build next, based on how people use it




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - A designer's eye. You notice when a layout, a line, or an edit is off, and you fix it. Show us through a portfolio, side projects, or tools you've built.

 - Experience running LLM agents in production: tool use, MCP, prompt and skill design, evals, and the failures that only show up with real users

 - Experience building media pipelines with tools like ffmpeg, rendering engines, or generative image and video models

 - Five or more years as a software engineer. You are comfortable with the traditional full stack tool chain. You build with agents every day now, and you still have the fundamentals to review their code, debug it, and design systems that hold up.

 - Clear writing, for engineers and designers alike

Nice to Have

 - Experience with the Figma Plugin API or building on other design tools

 - A background in design, motion, film, or advertising

 - Internal tools you've built that people outside engineering chose to use

desc: The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values. The Fire Department, City of New York (FDNY), seeks a full-time City Research Scientist in the Bureau of OSHA. Reporting directly to the OSHA Director, the City Research Scientist will conduct environmental, health and safety audits of facilities and/or operations to ensure compliance with federal, state or local regulations and policies; prepare technical reports that identify deficiencies and provide recommended corrective actions; research local, state and federal laws and regulations to determine applicability to facilities and/or operations; ensure compliance with OSHA and NYS Department of Labor (PESH) regulations; make and record observations on the progress of research investigations and evaluate data; assist in the agency’s research efforts and environmental, health and safety issues, and other research projects; conduct workplace assessments/audits/investigations and understand industrial processes; collect and analyze occupational illness and injury data; perform air monitoring and/or other industrial hygiene measurements utilizing a variety of technical equipment; assist OSHA Director with research and presentations; responsible for data gathering and various technical and administrative tasks.
